newsitem.title: EGYPT: U.S. vote on Jerusalem unwise - Egypt.
newsitem.headline: U.S. vote on Jerusalem unwise - Egypt.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak said in remarks on Friday that a U.S. House of Representatives resolution calling on President Bill Clinton to reaffirm that Jerusalem must remain Israel's undivided capital was "unwise".
Israel, which captured Arab East Jerusalem in 1967 and annexed it in a move unrecognised by the international community including the United States, has welcomed Tuesday's 406-17 vote.

Mubarak was quoted by the official daily Al-Akhbar newspaper as saying: "The resolution was unwise, especially that it came at a time when the peace process was passing through a crisis, which would escalate the situation."

The Egyptian president made his remarks at a joint news conference with Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi in the Libyan coastal northeastern city of Tobruk, where he arrived on Thursday for a two-day visit.

The vote, which does not oblige the Clinton administration to act, came as Egypt struggled to resolve a peacemaking crisis between Israel and the PLO spurred by Israel's beginning work in March on a 6,500-home Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
The Palestinians, who regard East Jerusalem as the capital of a future state, said the U.S. House resolution was a declaration of war.

In October 1995, the U.S. Senate and the House passed the Jerusalem Embassy Act which states as a matter of U.S. policy that Jerusalem should remain "the undivided capital of Israel" and that the American embassy should be moved there by May 1999.
But, recognising the volatility of the issue of Jerusalem, it allowed Clinton to suspend the embassy's move from Tel Aviv for six-month periods.
Costa Rica and El Salvador are the only countries with embassies in Jerusalem.
